newsitem.title: USA: Miami arena referendum upheld by appeals court.
newsitem.headline: Miami arena referendum upheld by appeals court.

text.p: A referendum on Dade County's new bond-financed arena for the Miami Heat will take place as scheduled on Nov 5, Florida's Third District Court of Appeals ruled.

Opponnets of the arena plan collected enough petition signatures to force the referendum. But the bsketball team sued last month to block the vote, claiming the ballot language was confusing and illegally addressed more than one topic.
Dade County Circuit Court Judge Ronald Freidman refused to rule until after the polls close on Nov 5, so the team appealed to the higher court.

In a ruling Thursday, the appeals court rejected the Heat's arguments. A three-judge panel said the ballot language was valid, and that Dade County's charter did not limit referendums to a single topic.
The appeals court sent the case back to Friedman with instructions to dismiss the complaint.
Attorney Dan Paul, who led the petition drive to force the referendum, said "I hope the Heat will now cease this arrogant attempt to prevent the issue from going before voters."
Heat attorney Bruce Rogow said the team was unlikly to appeal to the Florida Supreme Court before the election, although it may do so afterward depending on the outcome of a similar case.
The Heat has agreed to pay $50 million toward the arena and the county plans to finance the rest via a Miami Sports Authority revenue bond issue backed by hotel taxes.
